jesus_905.summary: Jesus is the central figure of the Gospels, born to Mary and proclaimed as the Christ. The Gospels recount his teaching, healings, crucifixion, and resurrection; Acts describes his ascension and the witness of his followers.

jesus_904.summary: Jesus, surnamed Justus, was a Jewish Christian whom Paul names among his fellow workers. He is distinct from Jesus Christ.

mary_1938.summary: Mary was the mother of Jesus and the wife of Joseph. Luke describes Gabriel’s announcement, Jesus’ birth, and Mary’s response; Acts includes her among the believers gathered in prayer.

mary_1939.summary: Mary of Bethany was the sister of Martha and Lazarus. She listened at Jesus’ feet and later anointed him before his death.

mary_1940.summary: This Mary is identified as the mother of James and Joses. Matthew places her among the women who witnessed the crucifixion and watched Jesus’ burial.

mary_1941.summary: Mary was the mother of John, also called Mark. Believers gathered to pray in her Jerusalem home, where Peter came after his release from prison.

mary_1942.summary: Mary was a Christian in Rome whom Paul greeted with appreciation for her much labour. The passage does not identify her with the other women named Mary.

mary_1943.summary: Mary Magdalene followed Jesus after being delivered from seven devils. She witnessed his crucifixion and burial and reported the risen Jesus to his disciples.

john_1676.summary: John the Baptist preached repentance and baptized in the Jordan. He prepared the way for Jesus, baptized him, and was later imprisoned and executed by Herod.

john_1677.summary: John, the son of Zebedee and brother of James, was one of Jesus’ twelve apostles. Acts describes him teaching with Peter and sharing in the early church’s witness.

john_1678.summary: John is named among the high priest’s kindred at the Jerusalem hearing of Peter and John. This record is distinct from the apostle John and John the Baptist.

mark_1679.summary: John, surnamed Mark, was the son of Mary of Jerusalem. He accompanied Barnabas and Saul, later travelled with Barnabas, and is named by Paul as useful for ministry.

joseph_1715.summary: Joseph, a descendant of David, was Mary’s husband. Matthew describes his response to the angel’s message, his care for Jesus, and the family’s flight to Egypt and return to Nazareth.

joseph_1716.summary: Joseph of Arimathaea was a disciple who asked Pilate for Jesus’ body. He wrapped it in linen and placed it in his own new tomb.

james_717.summary: James, the son of Zebedee and brother of John, was one of the twelve apostles. Herod killed him with the sword, as recorded in Acts.

james_718.summary: James, the son of Alphaeus, is named among Jesus’ twelve apostles. His patronymic distinguishes him from James the son of Zebedee.

james_719.summary: James is named among Jesus’ brothers. Paul also mentions James, the Lord’s brother, and Acts presents James taking a leading role in the Jerusalem church.

herod_1504.summary: Herod was king of Judaea when Jesus was born. Matthew recounts his questioning of the wise men and his order to kill the young children in Bethlehem.

lazarus_1811.summary: Lazarus is the poor man in Jesus’ account of the rich man and Lazarus. He lay at the rich man’s gate and, after death, was carried by angels into Abraham’s bosom. He is distinct from Lazarus of Bethany.

lazarus_1812.summary: Lazarus of Bethany was the brother of Mary and Martha. John recounts his illness, death, and restoration to life when Jesus called him out of the tomb.

martha_1937.summary: Martha was the sister of Mary and Lazarus of Bethany. She welcomed Jesus, served him, and confessed that he was the Christ before Lazarus was raised.

priscilla_2370.summary: Priscilla and her husband Aquila worked with Paul as tentmakers and travelled with him. Together they explained the way of God more fully to Apollos.

aquila_279.summary: Aquila was a Jew born in Pontus, the husband of Priscilla, and a tentmaker. He worked with Paul, and with Priscilla instructed Apollos more fully.

ruth_2450.summary: Ruth was a Moabite widow who remained with her mother-in-law Naomi and went to Bethlehem. She married Boaz and became the mother of Obed, the grandfather of David.

boaz_519.summary: Boaz was a man of Bethlehem, a relative of Naomi’s husband Elimelech. He protected Ruth as she gleaned, acted as kinsman in the family’s redemption, and married her.

naomi_2147.summary: Naomi was the wife of Elimelech and mother of Mahlon and Chilion. After their deaths in Moab, she returned to Bethlehem with Ruth and helped arrange Ruth’s marriage to Boaz.

hannah_1400.summary: Hannah was a wife of Elkanah and the mother of Samuel. She prayed for a son, dedicated Samuel to the LORD, and brought him to serve at Shiloh.

samuel_2469.summary: Samuel was the son of Elkanah and Hannah, dedicated to the LORD at Shiloh. He served as prophet and judge, and anointed both Saul and David as king.

esther_1343.summary: Esther, also called Hadassah, was a Jewish woman raised by her cousin Mordecai who became queen to Ahasuerus. She risked approaching the king to plead for her people against Haman’s decree.

mordecai_2107.summary: Mordecai was a Jew of the tribe of Benjamin who raised his cousin Esther. He uncovered a plot against the king, resisted Haman, and helped secure deliverance for the Jews.

daniel_975.summary: Daniel was among the Judaean captives brought to Babylon. The book bearing his name describes his service under foreign kings, interpretation of dreams, visions, and rescue from the lions’ den.

ezekiel_1237.summary: Ezekiel was a priest, the son of Buzi, among the captives by the river Chebar. His book records visions and prophetic messages concerning judgment, exile, and restoration.

isaiah_617.summary: Isaiah, the son of Amoz, prophesied concerning Judah and Jerusalem. His book describes his call, messages of judgment and hope, and his counsel to King Hezekiah.

jeremiah_853.summary: Jeremiah, the son of Hilkiah, was a priest from Anathoth called to prophesy to Judah. His ministry spanned the final kings of Judah and Jerusalem’s fall to Babylon.

nehemiah_2172.summary: Nehemiah, the son of Hachaliah, served as cupbearer to King Artaxerxes. He obtained permission to return to Jerusalem, led the rebuilding of its walls, and served as governor.

ezra_1245.summary: Ezra was a priest and scribe skilled in the law of Moses. He led a return from Babylon to Jerusalem and taught the law to the returned community.

deborah_996.summary: Deborah was Rebekah’s nurse. Genesis records her death and burial beneath an oak near Bethel; she is distinct from Deborah the judge.

deborah_997.summary: Deborah was a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, and a judge in Israel. She summoned Barak to battle against Sisera, accompanied him, and celebrated the victory in song.

gideon_1314.summary: Gideon, also called Jerubbaal, was the son of Joash. Called to deliver Israel from Midian, he tore down his father’s altar to Baal and led a force reduced to three hundred men.

samson_2468.summary: Samson was the son of Manoah, set apart as a Nazarite from birth. Judges recounts his strength, conflicts with the Philistines, betrayal by Delilah, and final destruction of their temple.

delilah_1005.summary: Delilah was a woman in the valley of Sorek whom Samson loved. At the Philistine rulers’ urging, she sought the secret of his strength and arranged his capture.

rahab_2388.summary: Rahab was a woman of Jericho who hid Joshua’s spies and helped them escape. She and her household were spared when Israel took the city.

bathsheba_416.summary: Bathsheba was the daughter of Eliam and wife of Uriah. David took her while Uriah was away at war; after Uriah’s death she became David’s wife and later the mother of Solomon.

uriah_2898.summary: Uriah the Hittite was Bathsheba’s husband and one of David’s mighty men. David ordered him placed in the fiercest fighting and abandoned there, resulting in his death.

solomon_2762.summary: Solomon was the son of David and Bathsheba who succeeded David as king. He was known for wisdom and built the temple at Jerusalem; Kings also recounts his later turning toward other gods.

saul_2478.summary: Saul, the son of Kish of Benjamin, became Israel’s first king. Samuel anointed him; his reign included conflict with the Philistines, his pursuit of David, and his death at Mount Gilboa.

andrew_264.summary: Andrew was Simon Peter’s brother and one of Jesus’ twelve apostles. John describes him bringing Simon to Jesus and pointing out the boy with five loaves and two fishes.

philip_2344.summary: Philip was one of the twelve apostles. John recounts his call, his invitation to Nathanael to meet Jesus, and his request to be shown the Father.

philip_2347.summary: Philip was one of the seven chosen to serve the Jerusalem believers. He preached in Samaria and explained Isaiah to the Ethiopian eunuch; Acts later calls him the evangelist.

philip_2345.summary: Philip is identified as the brother of Herod and the husband of Herodias before she married Herod. He is distinct from Philip the apostle and Philip the tetrarch.

philip_2346.summary: Philip was tetrarch of Ituraea and the region of Trachonitis when John the Baptist began his ministry. Luke identifies him as a brother of Herod the tetrarch.

luke_1836.summary: Luke was a companion of Paul, called the beloved physician in Colossians. Paul names him among his remaining companions in 2 Timothy and among his fellow labourers in Philemon.

barnabas_1722.summary: Barnabas, also called Joses, was a Levite from Cyprus. He supported the Jerusalem believers, introduced Saul to the apostles, and travelled with Paul in missionary work.

silas_2740.summary: Silas was a leading believer and prophet in the Jerusalem church. He carried its letter to Antioch and later travelled with Paul, sharing imprisonment at Philippi.

dorcas_2810.summary: Dorcas, also called Tabitha, was a disciple in Joppa known for good works and almsgiving. Acts recounts her death and Peter’s prayer before she was restored to life.

stephen_2802.summary: Stephen was one of the seven chosen to serve the Jerusalem believers. After speaking before the council, he was stoned; Acts describes him praying for those killing him.

cornelius_956.summary: Cornelius was a Roman centurion in Caesarea, described as devout and generous. He summoned Peter, whose message to his household was followed by their receiving the Holy Ghost and baptism.

nicodemus_2204.summary: Nicodemus was a Pharisee and ruler of the Jews who came to Jesus by night. He later questioned the judgment against Jesus and helped Joseph of Arimathaea prepare Jesus’ body for burial.

ananias_258.summary: Ananias and his wife Sapphira sold a possession and withheld part of the price while presenting the gift to the apostles. Acts recounts their deaths after Peter confronted their deception.

ananias_259.summary: Ananias was a disciple in Damascus sent by the Lord to Saul after his vision on the road. He laid hands on Saul, who regained his sight and was baptized.

ananias_260.summary: Ananias was the high priest before whom Paul appeared. Acts recounts his order to strike Paul and his later appearance with the elders to accuse Paul before Felix.

sapphira_2472.summary: Sapphira was the wife of Ananias. She agreed with him to withhold part of the proceeds of their sale and died after Peter questioned her about the price.

zacchaeus_2961.summary: Zacchaeus was a wealthy chief publican in Jericho who climbed a sycomore tree to see Jesus. After welcoming Jesus into his home, he promised generosity to the poor and restitution for fraud.

zipporah_3095.summary: Zipporah was the daughter of the priest of Midian and the wife of Moses. Exodus names her sons Gershom and Eliezer and recounts her action during the journey to Egypt.

zophar_3105.summary: Zophar the Naamathite was one of the three friends who came to comfort Job. His speeches appear in Job 11 and 20; the closing chapter includes him among those directed to offer sacrifice.

caleb_537.summary: Caleb, the son of Jephunneh, represented Judah among the spies sent into Canaan. He urged Israel to enter the land and later received Hebron as his inheritance.

joshua_893.summary: Joshua, also called Jeshua, was the son of Jozadak and high priest of the returned community. He worked with Zerubbabel to restore worship and rebuild the temple.

thomas_2851.summary: Thomas, also called Didymus, was one of Jesus’ twelve apostles. John describes his resolve to accompany Jesus to Judaea, his questions at the last supper, and his confession after seeing the risen Jesus.
